newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BTP volatility steady despite EMU nerves.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BTP volatility steady despite EMU nerves.

text.p: Implied volatility of BTP options on LIFFE was steady on Tuesday despite jitters in the underlying contract as monetary union worries resurfaced, traders said.

Ten-year Italian bonds have lost 16 basis points to Bunds so far this week in the cash market, as nagging doubts about Italy's entry into the first round of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) have taken their toll.

Germany's Ifo research institute said on Monday Italy may hit the EMU deficit target but it should be kept out of the first round of euro members because it lacked the sustainability required for monetary union.
In addition, one of Germany's "wise men" said over the weekend a pact between Germany and France to delay the planned 1999 start to EMU could not be ruled out.
The 10-year cash spread widened from 82 basis points at Friday's close to 98 basis points early on Tuesday. It was at 94 basis points at 1200 GMT.
But dealers said the impact on BTP options was negligible.
"There's not really much happening -- in terms of volatility, things are pretty steady," said one trader at a French house.
Dealers said September volatility at the 137.50 straddle was around 6.6 percent by mid-morning, unchanged from late Monday. December volatility was quoted at 6.90 percent.
By 1200 GMT, the September BTP future was up 14 basis points at 137.63, off an earlier low of 137.15.
One trader said there had been some two-way trade in 140.00 call options, with around 600 lots traded on the day. He also noted some interest in a 139.00, 140.00, 141.00 call butterfly.
"That's probably the most exciting trade out there at the moment," he said.
A butterfly trade occurs when you buy a call, sell two calls at a higher strike then buy another call at an equally higher strike.
